Steam profile: https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198163986648/ My matchmaking restriction dates back to 2019. I continued queuing because I really wanted to play, which led to Low Priority penalties and eventually a permanent matchmaking restriction. I understand that I was responsible for queuing with an unstable connection, and I am not denying the impact of my abandons on other players. This is my original Dota 2 account, and I would genuinely like to return to playing on it. Steam Support has confirmed that they will not lift the restriction. I respectfully ask whether the Dota 2 team could review my case and consider whether there is any possibility of reinstating matchmaking access. Description Hi Valve, Please take action against forms of toxic behavior that waste other players’ time and ruin matches. 1. Ward abuse A player places an observer ward in their own base within the first 10 minutes → 1-day matchmaking ban. A player places more than 4 sentry wards → same penalty. After the ban: Low Priority, 15 games to be played in Single Draft, with +5 minutes added to the average queue time. 2. Blocking allies’ retreat Add a new report category: “Blocked allied heroes’ retreat”. Verification: the report is checked automatically, e.g. an allied hero with low HP is moving away from enemies and is repeatedly body-blocked by the reported player’s hero, or confirmed by reports from several teammates. If confirmed, the player gets a notice: “You blocked your allies’ retreat”, a 1.5-hour matchmaking ban and 1 game in Single Draft. Why: this behavior is easy to detect, has almost no legitimate use, and costs the other players games. Please respect your players’ time and make the game less toxic. Dear Dota 2 Development Team / Steam Support, I am writing to report a critical database synchronization bug within the Conduct Summary system. A newly generated summary row was completely overwritten and rolled back in real-time by a subsequent match server, resulting in an erroneous, instant loss of 1,000 Behavior Score (BS) points, a 24-hour matchmaking ban, and Low Priority status. Account and Match Context (Timeline of the Bug on October 3rd, 2026): 1. The Correct Update: I finished a 15-game block. At 09:33 GMT, Conduct Summary #9027024387 was initially generated. My score increased by roughly +341 points from the previous 1954 BS, correctly displaying 2295 BS in my profile. 2. The Overwrite Trigger: Immediately after, I joined a new match as Phantom Assassin (PA). This match suffered from severe server-side lag and ping spikes (up to 150ms). I did not disconnect, did not abandon, and completed the match normally. 3. The Rollback Error: Instantly upon returning to the main menu after the PA match, the system did not create a new log entry. Instead, it retroactively modified the already generated Summary #9027024387. The final Behavior Score value was altered from 2295 to 1297, while leaving the game metrics completely clean (0 reports, 0 abandons). Full Account Historical Data (Proof of Contradiction): Here is the exact data extracted from my personal game logs, demonstrating that a perfect 15-game block resulted in a massive score drop due to the overwrite: MatchID Date (GMT) Periodic Ex.Reports Ex.Abandons MatchCount Positive Reported Abandoned Reports Commends BehaviorScore [BEFORE THE PA MATCH - ORIGINAL RECORD (Captured at 08:13:46 GMT)] MatchID Date (GMT) Periodic Ex.Reports Ex.Abandons MatchCount Positive Reported Abandoned Reports Commends BehaviorScore 9027024387 2026-10-03 08:13:46 Yes No No 15 15 0 0 0 35 2297 [AFTER THE PA MATCH - OVERWRITTEN RECORD (Captured at 09:33:47 GMT)] MatchID Date (GMT) Periodic Ex.Reports Ex.Abandons MatchCount Positive Reported Abandoned Reports Commends BehaviorScore 9027024387 2026-10-03 09:33:47 Yes No No 15 15 0 0 0 35 1297 <-- [CRITICAL DATABASE OVERWRITE BUG] [HISTORICAL DATA FOR REFERENCE] 9024012628 2026-10-01 06:55:59 Yes No No 15 15 0 0 0 29 1954 9020140670 2026-09-28 12:18:32 No Yes No 15 14 1 0 2 30 1804 9016058521 2026-09-25 20:58:18 Yes No No 15 13 2 0 6 31 2654 9013653323 2026-09-24 10:20:11 Yes No No 15 15 0 0 0 38 2404 This is an evident write-conflict / race condition between the primary behavior score calculation service and the individual match-ending script. ### Description ## Incorrect Abandon Records — Request for Manual Review and Penalty Removal ### Summary I am reporting what appears to be an incorrect recording of **Abandon** matches on my Dota 2 account. I have to guess from when my Low Priority games started. Losing a lane is not a crime. 4. **Party stacks have too much power against solo players.** A group that is losing can easily push a solo player into Overwatch. 5. **It is a death spiral.** The lower my score, the worse my teammates, the more often games collapse, the more reports I get, the lower my score. If possible, please review my account and my recent convictions. I am writing this not just for myself, but because I see many players with exactly the same story. Please fix this system. Description I am filing this report to formally contest three consecutive Overwatch convictions that came from human reviewers, not from any automated flag, issued under the griefing category, commonly referred to as trolling, which is the only category that could conceivably apply to what happened in my games. None of these convictions match what I actually did. I stayed for the full duration of each match, played my role, did not feed, did not abuse abilities against my own team, did not script, and did not troll in any sense of the word. These three convictions cover four match numbers, since I have no way of knowing for certain which of two specific matches triggered the third one. The first conviction corresponds to match 9005713707, played on September 19, 2026. The second corresponds to match 9008919256, played on September 20, 2026. For the third, I am attaching both candidate matches, 9011897482 and 9011927420, played on September 22, 2026 an hour apart. In all four matches there were teammates or opponents who evidently did not like the way I played. I stayed for the full duration in all four, and in none of them did the team's loss depend on me; when the team won, on the other hand, it won partly thanks to my cooperation. I am attaching screenshots from each of these four matches showing full attendance along with performance statistics that are consistent with normal, competitive play and inconsistent with griefing. I am also prepared to provide the replay files if that would help a human reviewer, Valve employee, or anyone with the authority to look at this case directly. I want to note that I have personally reviewed hundreds of Overwatch cases as a community reviewer, deciding each time whether the reported behavior actually amounted to griefing. That experience is exactly why these three verdicts are difficult to reconcile: the standard I apply when reviewing other players' matches does not match the standard that was apparently applied to mine. And this is not an isolated problem limited to my case: any player can report another simply because something personally annoyed them, without that implying an actual violation. Someone can report a teammate for trolling because they stole a last hit on a creep, or because that player did not play the way they personally would have liked, and that report reaches review with the same weight as a report over an actual violation. That is why any serious review of these cases should rest on a clear and strict rule: what gets sanctioned has to be universally sanctionable, not something that is only sanctionable according to the judgment of whoever filed the report or whoever reviewed that particular case. Universally sanctionable means that, in any possible context and under any reasonable interpretation, that way of playing is evidently trolling, not a forced reading of a normal play. Intentionally getting yourself killed falls into that category. Persistently stealing farm from the hard carry, ignoring roles and with no tactical reason, also falls into it. Clearly and consistently not respecting your role, for example staying in the jungle for forty minutes without leaving, whether you are the hard carry or a support, is also universally sanctionable. What does not fall into that category is, for example, a support not itemizing the way another player thinks they should, because the build in each match depends on how that specific match unfolds and is not a fixed standard. Reports like that should not even reach the review stage, let alone turn into a conviction. On top of that, there is no channel through which Steam Support can manually review, at the request of the sanctioned player, the exact moment of the match that was reported for trolling. The convicted player is given no timestamp, no description of the reported action, and no explanation of what led a reviewer to a guilty verdict, and there is no way to ask anyone to look at that specific moment again. Three consecutive convictions under those conditions, with no way to see the reasoning behind them and no way to ask for them to be reconsidered, amount to a punitive system with no accountability toward the people it judges. I am not claiming every Overwatch verdict is wrong. My complaint is specific: whoever reviewed these three cases did not apply any universally sanctionable standard, and having reviewed hundreds of cases myself, I know what that standard looks like in practice. If the same account received three wrong convictions in a row, whatever led reviewers to reach that verdict deserves scrutiny on its own, independent of whether any single case would have been overturned on individual appeal. I am formally requesting a manual review of the matches mentioned above by Valve, carried out by someone with direct access to the original reports, the reviewer decisions, and the full replays of the three convictions, with specific access to the exact moment reported in each case, and with the outcome communicated back to me directly rather than left as a silent score adjustment. Every piece of evidence I have access to as a player is included here or available on request. What I am asking for is a genuine review of the three cases that led to this point, under a standard that clearly distinguishes real trolling from a play that someone simply did not like. ### Example Description Hello Valve / Dota 2 Team, I am reporting a problem with the current Overwatch and behavior restriction system and, more specifically, the lack of transparency or an appeal/review mechanism for players who receive an Overwatch conviction. I have been playing Dota 2 since November 4, 2012, and this account has been part of my gaming history for almost 14 years. Recently, my Behavior Score dropped from 7,987 to 3,077 in a relatively short period of time. During this period I received multiple Low Priority penalties, and my communication features were eventually disabled. The most recent penalty was particularly concerning because it was issued after an Overwatch review. The match in question is: Match ID: 9001535070 Hero: Outworld Destroyer Result: Victory Score: 23 / 4 / 15 MVP Reports: 2 Commends: 28 After contacting Steam Support, I specifically asked them to investigate what happened to my account or, if Steam Support could not investigate Overwatch decisions, to provide me with a way to contact the team responsible for reviewing them. Steam Support confirmed that the matchmaking restriction was caused by an Overwatch conviction and later confirmed that the conviction was based on this exact match (9001535070). However, Steam Support also told me that: - they do not review or remove Overwatch restrictions; - they cannot provide contact information for the Overwatch team; - and there is no alternative appeal channel they can provide. I understand that Steam Support may not have the ability to manually remove an Overwatch restriction. I am not asking for special treatment or for Valve to simply remove my penalty because I disagree with it. My concern is the lack of transparency. If an Overwatch conviction is based on a specific match, I believe the affected player should at least be able to understand what behavior was considered a violation. At the moment, I have no information about: 1. What specific behavior in match 9001535070 resulted in the conviction. 2. What category of violation was identified. 3. What part or timestamp of the replay was considered evidence. 4. Whether the conviction was reviewed by multiple reviewers or how the verdict was validated. 5. Whether there is any mechanism to challenge an incorrect Overwatch verdict. I fully understand that a good KDA, winning a match, or receiving MVP does not automatically prove that no violation occurred. I am therefore not claiming that my statistics alone prove the conviction was wrong. The problem is that I have no way to determine what I supposedly did wrong in the first place. This is especially concerning because the affected player cannot meaningfully learn from or challenge a decision when the only information provided is that an Overwatch conviction occurred. There is also an important context regarding my recent Behavior Score history. Between two of my recent conduct summaries, my Behavior Score changed from 3,902 to 3,077. During those seven matches I won 6 out of 7 games. The final match in that sequence was the Outworld Destroyer game mentioned above, which was a 23/4/15 victory with 28 commends and 2 reports. Again, I am not presenting this as proof that the Overwatch verdict must be wrong. I am providing it because the circumstances make it particularly important for me to understand what behavior was actually reviewed and why it resulted in a conviction. I am also a long-time Dota 2 streamer and content creator. Because I regularly stream my games, I have experienced situations where viewers or other players intentionally watch the stream and interact with the game around it. I cannot prove that this caused the reports or the Overwatch conviction, so I am not presenting it as a fact. However, I believe it is a relevant possibility when investigating unusual reporting patterns on a streaming account. I am not asking Valve to reveal the identities of Overwatch reviewers or any private information about them. I am asking for a reasonable way for an affected player to understand and, when appropriate, challenge an Overwatch decision. My questions to the Dota 2 team are therefore: - Is there currently any way for a player to obtain information about the specific violation that resulted in an Overwatch conviction? - Is there any mechanism for reviewing or appealing a potentially incorrect Overwatch verdict? - How does Valve ensure that Overwatch convictions are sufficiently validated before they result in matchmaking restrictions and major Behavior Score penalties? - If a conviction is found to be incorrect, is there any mechanism to correct the resulting Behavior Score or other penalties? I have been playing Dota 2 for almost 14 years and I genuinely do not want to leave the game because of a punishment that I cannot understand or challenge. I would appreciate it if the Dota 2 team could clarify how this system is intended to work from the perspective of the player receiving the conviction. Thank you. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) 9001535070 ### Screenshots My Dota 2 account has been permanently restricted from matchmaking since approximately 2019. My last Dota 2 match was played in 2019, meaning that this restriction is now approximately seven years old. I have contacted Steam Support multiple times regarding this restriction. Each time, I received the same standard response stating that the Dota team determined that the account had engaged in one or more forms of negative behavior and that Steam Support would not lift the restriction. I understand the reason that has been provided to me. I am not asking for confidential information about Valve's detection systems, and I am not asking Steam Support to repeat the same explanation again. My request is for an actual manual review of this old restriction. I have specifically asked Steam Support to escalate my case to a senior representative or the Dota team, but my requests have been answered with the same standard response and the ticket has been closed. The original restriction message indicated negative behavior such as: - A consistent pattern of user reports, negative conduct, and player abuse - Feeding - Abandoning - Non-participation in matches At the time, I also had an unstable internet connection, which could cause disconnects and low-priority penalties. I acknowledge that I may have made mistakes in the past, and I am not trying to deny the possibility of negative behavior from that period. However, approximately seven years have now passed. I have not played Dota 2 since 2019. My internet connection and hardware are stable now, and I would like to return to Dota 2. I am not asking Valve to ignore its rules or disclose internal enforcement information. I am asking whether the Dota team can manually review an approximately seven-year-old permanent restriction and reconsider whether I can be given one opportunity to return to matchmaking. I can provide screenshots of my previous Steam Support conversations showing the repeated standard responses and my requests for escalation. Thank you for taking the time to read this and consider my request. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) _No response_ ### Screenshots Description ### Description I encountered a VAC-related issue that prevented me from reconnecting to an ongoing ranked match after Dota 2 crashed. Some time ago, I accidentally deleted the normal Dota 2 desktop shortcut created by Steam. Instead of recreating the standard Steam shortcut, I manually added a shortcut by browsing to the Dota 2 executable and placing that shortcut on my desktop. On September 17, 2026, I launched Dota 2 through this manually created desktop shortcut. Everything initially worked normally: - Steam was running. - Dota 2 launched normally. - I was able to search for a public ranked match. - VAC did not display any warning before matchmaking. - I connected to the match and played normally. Near the end of the match, when the game was already close to being won, Dota 2 crashed after Alt+Tab. I immediately relaunched Dota 2 and attempted to reconnect to the same match. At this point, I received the following message: "Valve Anti-Cheat was unable to verify the reliability of your device. If you do not resolve this issue, online play may be unavailable." Because of this VAC verification error, I could not reconnect to the ongoing match. I tried: - Restarting Dota 2 several times. - Restarting Steam. - Restarting my PC. - Checking my Windows security configuration. My system security configuration was: - Windows 11 64-bit - Secure Boot: Enabled - TPM version: 2.0 The issue was finally resolved when I stopped launching Dota 2 through the manually created shortcut and instead launched Dota 2 directly from my Steam Library. After launching the exact same Dota 2 installation from the Steam Library, VAC verification worked normally again. No changes were made to Windows, BIOS, TPM, Secure Boot, game files or hardware between the failed VAC verification and the successful launch from the Steam Library. ### Why this appears to be a bug The important part is that Dota 2 / VAC allowed me to: 1. Launch the game using this shortcut. 2. Enter matchmaking. 3. Accept a ranked match. 4. Connect to a VAC-secured server. 5. Play almost the entire match normally. However, after the client crashed, the same launch method caused VAC to reject the device and prevented me from reconnecting to the match. If launching Dota 2 directly through this type of shortcut is not considered valid by VAC, I believe the game should detect this before the player is allowed to enter matchmaking. Allowing the player to enter a ranked match normally and then preventing them from reconnecting after a client crash can cause an unavoidable abandon and ranked / behavior penalties. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Delete or do not use the standard Dota 2 Steam desktop shortcut. 2. Manually create a desktop shortcut by browsing to the Dota 2 executable. 3. Make sure Steam is running. 4. Launch Dota 2 using the manually created shortcut. 5. Search for and enter an online matchmaking game. 6. During the match, close or crash Dota 2. 7. Relaunch Dota 2 using the same manually created shortcut. 8. Attempt to reconnect to the match. 9. VAC may display: "Valve Anti-Cheat was unable to verify the reliability of your device." 10. Close Dota 2. 11. Launch Dota 2 directly from the Steam Library. 12. VAC verification works normally again. ### Expected behavior If Dota 2 allows a player to enter a VAC-secured ranked match, restarting the client during that match should not cause VAC to reject the same device solely because the game was launched through a different shortcut. Alternatively, if this method of launching Dota 2 is unsupported, the player should be warned or prevented from entering matchmaking before the match starts. ### Match information Match ID: 9003543610 Date: September 17, 2026 ### Additional software / system information Overwolf is installed on my PC and I use it for Path of Exile 2. I am including this only as additional system information and I am not claiming that Overwolf caused the issue. Secure Boot: Enabled TPM: 2.0 OS: Windows 11 64-bit ### Penalty / Match review request Because this issue occurred during an active ranked match and directly prevented me from reconnecting, I would appreciate it if the affected match could also be reviewed. I did not intentionally abandon the match. I attempted to reconnect immediately and repeatedly, including restarting the game and my PC. If an abandon, MMR loss, Behavior Score / Conduct Score reduction, matchmaking restriction, Low Priority penalty or any other automated penalty was applied specifically because I could not reconnect due to this VAC verification issue, please consider reversing or excluding that penalty if technically possible. Match ID: 9003543610 ### Attachments I have a screenshot of the VAC error showing: "Valve Anti-Cheat was unable to verify the reliability of your device." Support (Ari) directed me to post this here because the current Behavior Score system has a fundamental design flaw at the ~3k level. The way the communication ban interacts with automated reports creates an impossible, inescapable loop for players who are genuinely trying to win and improve their score. **The Core Design Flaw: Playing with Bots** Communication is the absolute core of any multiplayer team game. When you completely remove a player's ability to communicate, you turn a team-based strategic game into a single-player experience. I might as well be playing against bots, because the interaction with my team is exactly the same. When you drop below 6,000 behavior score, you cannot ask for help, coordinate with your team, ping the map effectively, or explain macro decisions. Because you cannot explain your actions, teammates lacking map awareness automatically assume you are griefing, report you, and the automated system issues severe punishments with zero human oversight. **Case Study from a Recent Match:** To demonstrate how this algorithm fails, here is exactly what happened in my recent match. I played Axe offlane with a Phoenix support against a very tough Spectre and Enchantress lane. Phoenix was role-abusing, taking farm and last hits instead of helping me survive. From a gameplay design perspective, what is the intended correct play here? - **Option A:** Stand at a safe distance on the lane, get zero gold, and leech experience from my support (who can safely solo the lane due to range and escape skills). This is widely considered griefing. - **Option B:** Leave the unplayable lane, move to the jungle to recover, and let the support have the lane. I chose Option B. I stopped contesting Phoenix for farm and went to jungle. Because I was completely muted by the system, I couldn't tell my team why I was doing this. Here is how the situation escalated: - Phoenix followed me to the jungle to steal last hits from a triple-stacked camp I made. - He/she then moved to the safe lane to stand in trees, doing nothing, but to leech XP from our carries. - He/she went in to bushes to AFK for about 15 seconds from a middle of teamfight with full hp. I ended up doing the supports (Phoenix) work, buying 3 Observers and 6 Sentries, while the actual support bought exactly 2 Sentries in a 42-minute game. I also made several immediate buybacks after dying. Again, because I was muted, I couldn't explain that this was a deliberate macro strategy. Returning to the lane meant instant death from Spectre and Enchantress. Buying back allowed me to farm safer areas and stay close to the game's overall XP progression. The scoreboard at the end of the game proves this strategy worked: I successfully kept up with the level progression and was on the exact same level as everyone else. Once I got the relevant basic items (Vanguard, Blink Dagger to counter the 4 ranged enemies, and a Blade Mail), I rotated back, tanked damage, initiated fights, and we actually won the game. I was even commended by our carries. **The Automated Punishment & The Single Draft Trap:** Despite adapting to a griefing teammate, buying the wards, playing to the very end, and winning the game, the automated system immediately hit me with a 4-hour matchmaking ban, a -500 behavior score drop, and a Low Priority penalty requiring 3 Single Draft wins to escape. This Single Draft penalty is completely contradictory and feeds directly into the same broken loop: - You are forced to play with actual, legitimate griefers who are in Low Priority for the right reasons. - Because the hero pool is restricted, teammates frequently pick unsuitable heroes for the lineup, leading to setups with 4 or 5 hard carries. - People refuse to adapt their roles, or they simply have never played the random heroes they were given. - This inevitably leads to more griefing, ruined games, and consequently, more false reports from tilted teammates. - As a result, your behavior score continues to tank even further based on false reports while you are just trying to win your 3 mandatory matches. I am a 37-year-old man, and I do not believe I have ever been a toxic player. I do not throw rage fits, and I have never abandoned a match midway through unless there was a power outage (which hasn't happened in years). I am a team player—in non-role queue games, if everyone else picks a carry or a tank, I will always try to pick a support or whatever role the team is missing. To be completely honest, I do not even remember why my behavior score originally dropped to ~3000, because it happened several years ago. Since then, due to how this communication ban and punishment loop operates, it has been practically impossible to raise it back up. **The Mathematical Impossibility:** The most broken part of this system is the math behind recovering your score: - **The Grind:** If you manage to play 15 games without a single negative ping or false report, the system updates your score by about 250 points. That is roughly 12.5 hours of playing. - **The Punishment:** After this single match—where I didn't communicate at all, adapted to a bad lane, and won the game—I lost 500 points. - **The Result:** 25 hours of clean grinding wiped out by an automated algorithm in an instant. My score dropped back to 2,500. Now, on top of a 4-hour ban and the Single Draft prison, I am forced to play AT LEAST another 25 hours of unranked games just to unlock ranked matchmaking again, just for the exact same problem to repeat. **The "For Fun" Report Exploit:** The vulnerability of this automated system is public knowledge. There are multiple YouTube videos right now showing players admitting they report others purely for fun. They proudly showcase their "Action Taken" lists on screen, openly acknowledging that none of the players they reported actually did anything wrong—yet your automated system still punishes those innocent players based on malicious reports. **Conclusion** I completely understand that a multiplayer game needs a punishment system to keep the community healthy, but this current implementation is absolutely not the right way to do it. How can a player improve their behavior score when the system mutes them from explaining legitimate gameplay decisions, forces them into an endless 25-hour grind for minimal points, traps them in Single Draft with actual griefers, and empowers those griefers to hand out automated bans? I have played Dota for 14 years, but I have completely lost faith in how this game and its automated systems are being managed. I used to absolutely hate League of Legends, but this complete lack of respect for your player base has forced me to reconsider. It has become glaringly obvious that Valve only values high-ranked and professional players, while us paying, casual players who actually fund the game are completely ignored. You are simply riding on the legend of the game at this point. This fundamentally broken system is undoubtedly driving many dedicated players to League of Legends, and I am now one of them. I will be canceling my long-term subscription upon making this transition. Description During this match, I repeatedly experienced "Restoring Dota 2 Game Coordinator" issues and was repeatedly disconnected from the game. My teammate in the same match was also experiencing the same connection/disconnection problem, so this did not appear to be an issue isolated to my connection or PC. After I managed to reconnect, the game was already in a broken state. Several important game elements and functions were no longer working correctly: Trees were completely missing from my game. I could not use or access Neutral Items. I could not purchase Aghanim's Shard. I continued experiencing repeated disconnections during the match. Because of the repeated disconnects, the game eventually recorded me as having abandoned the match. Despite these issues, I continued playing the match after reconnecting instead of intentionally leaving the game. Troubleshooting Attempted I tried several steps to resolve the issue during the incident: Exited Dota 2 completely and reopened the game. Exited Steam completely and reopened Steam. Verified the integrity of the Dota 2 game files through Steam. Reconnected to the match multiple times after being disconnected. However, the Game Coordinator/disconnection issue continued, and after reconnecting, the game still had the broken gameplay state described above. Expected Result The game should have maintained a normal game state after reconnecting, with trees, Neutral Items, the item shop, and other gameplay functions working normally. If the Game Coordinator/server was experiencing an issue affecting multiple players in the same match, the match should ideally not result in an abandon/low-priority penalty for players affected by the technical problem. Actual Result The Game Coordinator repeatedly entered a restoring state, causing repeated disconnections. After reconnecting, the game state was partially broken: trees were missing, Neutral Items could not be used, and I could not purchase Aghanim's Shard. The repeated disconnections eventually caused an abandon penalty. Additional Information My teammate was also experiencing repeated disconnections during the same match. In addition, the in-game chat appeared to be malfunctioning, as I could not see responses from my teammates and it appeared that they could not see my messages. I continued the match despite the technical issues and did not intentionally abandon it. I would appreciate it if the match could be reviewed and the resulting abandon/low-priority penalty could be reconsidered, as the penalty occurred after repeated Game Coordinator/disconnection Description Hello Valve / Dota 2 Team, I enjoy Dota and play it whenever I have free time. However, for several years now, I have been stuck in what feels like a nightmare of this game, with a Behavior Score fluctuating between 0 and 5,000. Since I don't play Ranked, I don't have the option to avoid parties. As many players know, party players tend to report solo players, shifting the blame for their own poor performance onto the one player who isn't in their group. This happens very often. Currently, I can't even reach 3,000 Behavior Score. It feels like the system intentionally places me in matches right when I'm about to hit that mark, matching me with a full party of four players — which means four reports. This leads me straight into Overwatch. And Overwatch, as it stands, almost always returns a guilty verdict. There are discussions where people admit they click "Guilty" on every case without reviewing the replay at all. As a result, you lose 1,000 points from the verdict, and the reports also throw you into Low Priority games, where you continue to get reported endlessly. In total, you lose around 1,500 points, and you're back to 1,000 Behavior Score. The cycle repeats endlessly, and there is simply no way out of it in the current state of the system. I see many other players reporting similar issues on your GitHub. About two months ago, I finally became so frustrated that I took a break after receiving 4 Low Priority games. I returned recently for the event and noticed that matchmaking had been reworked — I hoped the Behavior Score system had received some attention as well. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case. I struggled through those Low Priority games, managed to play 4 All Pick matches, and then received another punishment from Overwatch. In all 4 of those games, I was the only solo player on my team. There were constant pings directed at me, insults, and likely reports as well. I played well in all of those matches, and there was absolutely no valid reason for a penalty. I realize that nobody is going to review these games, but to support my claim, here is the Match ID from which I received the punishment: 8956143152. By the way, in that same match, the Terrorblade player destroys his items at 48:18. But naturally, no one will report him because he is playing with his friends in a party and can do whatever he wants — they are just having fun. I believe there are several ways to improve this system and potentially bring back hundreds, or even thousands, of players who have left because of these issues. For example: 1. Introduce a "Behavior Score Reset Token" as a reward in one of the events, at least once a year — for instance, in the Quartero's Curios event at level 150. This token would be non-tradable, non-giftable, and usable only once per account, setting the Behavior Score to its maximum value. Ruiners would drop back down in just a few games anyway, so this wouldn't harm normal players in any way. 2. Extend the "Avoid Party" feature to unranked matches, just as it already exists in Ranked. This would at least partially prevent situations where a solo player receives 4 reports and ends up in Overwatch, leading to automatic Low Priority games. 3. Increase the accountability and quality standards for Overwatch reviewers. Currently, there is no penalty for reviewers who hand out "Guilty" verdicts without properly reviewing the evidence. Implementing a quality check or a verification mechanism for Overwatch cases would ensure that only genuine griefers are punished, and innocent players are not caught in a faulty automated loop. I see many posts here about the flaws in the Behavior Score system, and I truly hope you take this feedback into consideration. Thank you for your time and for this incredible is a long-standing and very frustrating issue in Dota 2 related to the communication system and the Behavior Score system. When a player has a low behavior score, is in low priority, or is in a muted/punished chat pool (due to reports), the in-game chat becomes restricted or disabled. As a result, the /roll command (which generates a random number to resolve disputes) stops working in all modes, including normal non-role queue matches (All Pick without strict role assignment). What this leads to: Draft Chaos. When two players both want to play mid (or carry/offlane), they have no fair way to decide who gets the role. Double Mid Syndrome. Since /roll is unavailable, players just lock a second mid hero anyway, turning the game into a toxic mess from minute zero. Game Ruining. Instead of a civilized resolution, arguments escalate, players start flaming each other, and often intentionally feed or grief because the dispute is only resolved by "who picks faster". Inequality. This issue disproportionately affects players with low behavior scores — who are already in a bad spot. Instead of giving them tools to resolve conflicts peacefully (like rolling), the system takes that tool away, making matches even more unbearable and preventing them from recovering their score. The Core Problem: /roll is NOT a social chat message; it is a gameplay mechanic (a console/chat command) that returns a random integer. Muting chat or restricting communication should not affect gameplay commands, especially in non-role queue modes where /roll is the only civilized way to distribute roles. Proposed Solution: Make the /roll command available regardless of "Low Priority", "Muted", or "Low Behavior Score" status. Alternatively, add a "Roll" button directly to the hero selection UI that is always functional (similar to how it works in tournament/captain's mode drafts or custom lobbies). This is a critical quality-of-life improvement for the community that would significantly reduce toxicity and the number of ruined Valve/Dota 2 Team, I am writing to report a critical exploit that is being systematically abused in the 12v12 custom game (Arcade mode). This exploit traps all legitimate players in an endless loop, making it impossible to play or leave without penalty. How the exploit works (step by step): 1. Room filling stage – The abuser (a bot-controlled account, usually a brand-new Steam account with zero Dota 2 match history) joins the custom game lobby like any normal player. When the room reaches the required player count, the game automatically launches into the loading screen. 2. Loading screen stage – Once the loading screen starts, the abuser either disconnects intentionally or deliberately fails to load the map (simulating a timeout). As a result, all other players are stuck on the loading screen, waiting for the abuser to load – for the full timeout period (approximately 5–10 minutes). 3. No escape for normal players – During this waiting period, if any normal player tries to exit the loading screen, the system immediately marks them as an abandoner, applying a matchmaking cooldown or low-priority penalty. The abuser, however, suffers absolutely no penalty for disconnecting or failing to load. 4. Endless loop – After the timeout expires, the game recognises that the abuser did not load and reopens the lobby (since it was full). The abuser instantly rejoins, and the cycle repeats. Normal players are trapped indefinitely – forced to either wait through the timeout again and again, or take the abandon penalty to break free. Key observations: · The abuser can be kicked from the lobby, but they rejoin within milliseconds (clearly using a script). · These abuser accounts are always brand new, with no prior Dota 2 matches played – suggesting they are mass-created bots. · This abuse is happening persistently, day after day, and specifically targets popular custom games like 12v12. Why I believe this is not just trolling: Given the systematic nature, the use of freshly created bot accounts, and the goal of ruining one specific game to drive players away, I strongly suspect this is organised by competing game studios that host their own custom games in the Arcade. They are deliberately blocking rival rooms to frustrate players into abandoning their favourite game and switching to their own pay‑to‑win titles, which are laden with microtransactions. Impact on the community: This exploit is devastating. Legitimate players are being tortured with endless waiting, forced to either suffer the penalty or give up on a game they love. The 12v12 community is shrinking because many players have simply stopped trying to start a match. Our requests: 1. Fix the abandon penalty logic – Ensure that players who disconnect or fail to load during the loading screen receive the same penalty as those who exit voluntarily, and that their behaviour is tracked. 2. Implement a cooldown on rapid rejoin/leave actions – Limit the number of times an account can enter/leave a lobby within a short timeframe (e.g., 5 times per minute). 3. Investigate the accounts involved – Look into the batch of new accounts with zero match history that are repeatedly causing these timeouts; consider flagging them for suspicious behaviour. 4. Consider a minimum game requirement – Require accounts to have played a certain number of normal matches before they can join Arcade lobbies, to deter bot creation. I have Steam IDs, and screenshots of these accounts if you need them. Please help us – we are just ordinary players who want to enjoy 12v12 without being held hostage. Thank you for your attention to this serious issue. Description Title: Feedback / Suggestion: Behavior Score system needs real-time updating and better balance for isolated bad games Body: Hi Valve team, I’d like to share some feedback regarding the current Behavior & Communication Score system. Currently, receiving a summary every 15 games makes the system feel rigid and unfair. A player can play 14 great games, have 1 bad game (or get targeted by a toxic party/tilted teammates), and end up with a heavily penalized report or even low priority. One single bad match shouldn't outweigh two weeks of good behavior. Suggestions for improvement: Real-time updates (similar to modern mobile competitive games): Instead of waiting 15 games for a batch update, let every single match influence the score dynamically. Weighted Recency: Recent games should hold meaningful weight, but isolated incidents shouldn't drastically ruin an entire reporting period. Better Variance Protection: A single bad game out of 15 should be treated as an anomaly, not a trend. This change would make the system feel much more transparent, fair, and encouraging for players who are actively trying to maintain high behavior scores. Description Dear Valve, I would like to share my experience with the behavior score system because I genuinely feel something is not working correctly in my case. Over the last several days, my behavior score has continued to decrease even though I play alone, focus on winning, and do my best to help my team. I don't understand why this is happening. I currently cannot even use chat, so I have no way to be toxic through text or voice communication. Despite that, my behavior score dropped from around 5,000 to about 4,000, and I received a 24-hour matchmaking ban. After this ban expires, I will most likely be placed into Low Priority, even though I don't believe I've done anything to deserve it. The most frustrating part is that I'm not a smurf or someone trying to ruin matches. I'm actually a relatively new player who wants to improve at Dota 2. I spend time learning heroes, watching guides, and trying to become a better teammate and player. I queue for ranked matches completely solo. Very often I get teammates who intentionally grief, give up early, or are simply much less experienced. Even in those situations, I keep playing until the end and sometimes manage to carry the game and win anyway. I don't abandon matches, I don't intentionally feed, and I always try my best regardless of how difficult the game becomes. Because of this, it's very confusing to see my behavior score constantly going down. It feels like I am being punished for something I didn't do. If players are reporting me simply because they are angry after a match or because I played differently than they expected, I hope those reports are being reviewed fairly. I understand that the behavior system is important for keeping the community healthy, and I support that goal. However, I also hope there is a way to identify cases where legitimate players are incorrectly losing behavior score. I would sincerely appreciate it if someone could review my account and the reports against it. If there has been a mistake, I kindly ask if my behavior score could be restored. I truly enjoy Dota 2 and want to continue improving, climbing the ranked ladder, and being a positive member of the community. Thank you for taking the time to read my message, and thank you for continuing to support the game. Description ​The current Behavior Score system is detrimental to the Dota 2 experience. It fails to distinguish between unavoidable technical issues (power/internet outages, hardware failures) and intentional disruptive behavior. As a result, players are trapped in a "point of no return," where recovery is nearly impossible. ​The game is fundamentally a team-based experience, yet this system forces players into a state of "silent survival." Players are now terrified to use voice or text chat to coordinate, as any interaction can trigger retaliatory reports from teammates. This silence destroys the core of Dota 2, as communication is essential for team play. ​Furthermore, this system drives players to abandon their main accounts and create new ones, which devalues the competitive integrity of the game. ​Proposed Reforms: ​Remove the Hidden Behavior Score: Replace the current hidden point system with a transparent and predictable disciplinary model. ​Clear Penalties for Abandoning: Instead of a complex score reduction, implement direct consequences for technical issues. For example: 3 abandons = 5 games of Low Priority. ​Targeted Communication Bans: If a player receives reports from all 9 other players in a single match, they should receive a 48-hour communication ban. If the behavior persists, the punishment should escalate to Low Priority matches without access to chat for the purpose of "correction." ​Low Priority Revamp: Replace the mandatory "Single Draft" (SD) mode in Low Priority with "All Random" (AR). This makes the punishment less monotonous and keeps the game engaging, even for those serving time. ​Address Report Abuse and the Overwatch System: The current report system is heavily abused as a weapon against teammates. Furthermore, the "Overwatch" system is ineffective because reviewers often lack context or are biased, leading to unfair judgments. We need a system that filters out malicious, weaponized reports rather than penalizing any form of communication. ​The goal should be to encourage positive communication and team play, not to force players into "mute mode" or drive them away from the game entirely. I urge the development team to reconsider the current model in favor of a more transparent and fair disciplinary framework. Description Description: Hello Valve Team, I am writing to report a critical issue with the current Behavior and Overwatch system at high-skill brackets (5000+ MMR). The system is heavily flawed and actively allows toxic account buyers, boosted profiles, and low-ranked reviewers to ruin the experience for legitimate high-tier players. I have over 6,000 hours of playtime and my Behavior Score has consistently stayed around 11,200+. Drops were rare and only occurred due to real-world power outages. However, within just two weeks, my score plummeted to 6,900, and I received 3 Low-Priority penalties back-to-back without breaking any rules. Here is the core problem with the current mechanics at 5000+ MMR: 1. Account Buyers & Rank-Boosted Toxicity: 5000+ MMR should represent high-tier gameplay. Instead, it is flooded with account buyers and boosted players who lack basic game sense, refuse to communicate, or make terrible decisions. When a legitimate player tries to coordinate the team using voice chat, these players submit malicious reports purely out of spite or to shift the blame for their own poor performance. 2. Incompetent Overwatch Reviewers: The system allows lower-ranked players (whose understanding of high-level Dota is completely lacking) to review Overwatch cases for high-MMR matches. They evaluate high-tier item builds or non-meta draft choices based on their own low-rank templates, resulting in unjustified "Guilty" verdicts for griefing. 3. Automated LP Triggers: Just yesterday, after receiving a notification that my score dropped due to reports, I logged into the game today without playing a single match only to find myself with a 3-game Single Draft penalty. The system acts automatically based on raw report volume rather than factual gameplay abuse. Please review the matchmaking reporting system algorithms. Legitimate high-MMR players should not have their accounts restricted because of malicious reports from account buyers or the incorrect verdicts of low-skilled Overwatch reviewers. My Steam Profile: https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561199125201042/ Contact Email: gamertop663@gmail.com Match ID: [8882424106] Timestamp: Entire match (specifically during the laning stage and mid-game) Case Details: This was the final match right before I was automatically placed into Low Priority. He effectively fed gold to the enemy team the entire game. His final score of 9/9/3 is misleading, as he only secured those kills at the very end of the match while the rest of the team was trying to push the enemy Ancient without him. Throughout the match, I tried to communicate with him via voice chat without any aggression, calmly asking him to play with the team. Instead of listening, this player and other low-skill allies submitted malicious reports against me simply because I pointed out his lack of impact. This match is a prime example of how account buyers abuse the report system to penalize legitimate players who are just trying to coordinate the game. ### Example Match ID (and possibly Timestamp) Description # **The Current Player Behavior System Creates Silent Matches and Makes Recovery Nearly Impossible** I have been playing Dota 2 for many years, and I believe the current Player Behavior Summary system has serious flaws that are damaging the quality of matches and the social experience of the game. For nearly a year, my Behavior Score has remained around 3000. During this time, I have had very limited communication privileges, rarely communicate with other players, do not abandon matches, and do not intentionally grief games. Despite this, my score barely changes and meaningful recovery appears almost impossible. The main issue is that the system does not seem to adequately distinguish between intentional griefing and simply having a bad game. When a team loses, frustrated players often report their teammates. A player can make mistakes, have a poor performance, or simply be unlucky without intentionally ruining the match. However, those reports still contribute to a punishment system that can trap players at low Behavior Scores for extremely long periods of time. Another consequence is that many matches have become completely silent. Players are afraid to communicate because they fear reports and further penalties. Others have already lost access to communication features. As a result, matches often contain: * No leadership * No strategic discussion * No coordination * No planning * No meaningful social interaction Dota 2 is fundamentally a team game. Communication is one of its most important elements. A system designed to improve player behavior should not create an environment where players are afraid to speak. My questions to the Dota team are: 1. How does the system distinguish between intentional griefing and simply performing poorly? 2. How is a player expected to recover from a very low Behavior Score if reports continue to outweigh positive behavior? 3. Is the current system achieving its intended goal, or is it simply creating silent matches where players avoid communication altogether? I understand the need to punish toxic behavior, intentional griefing, and abusive communication. However, the current system appears excessively punitive and offers very little transparency regarding how players can realistically recover. Description When a player activates Smoke of Deceit, the in-game notification that appears in team chat ("[Player] used Smoke of Deceit" / smoke activation message) is being treated by the report system as a personal text-chat message sent by that player. Because of this, other players can report me for communication abuse (text chat / voice toxicity) based solely on the automated smoke notification — even though I have no access to text chat or voice communication at all. My communication is restricted (Communication Score: 5200), and I have never sent a chat message or used voice in these games. This is critical: in Dota, a communication report can only be submitted for voice toxicity or text-chat toxicity. Game-ruining behavior is tracked under a separate, general "Reports" metric (see column 10 in the attached statistics). The reports I am receiving are landing under the communication category (column 12) — which is logically impossible, because I have no communication access for which I could be reported. Timeline proving the bug The correlation is exact: toxicity reports against me started immediately after the Smoke update was released, even though I have never had chat access during that period. My text chat was only unlocked for a single short window: from 2026-06-05 13:46:59 GMT to 2026-06-08 17:43:51 GMT. Outside of that window, my Behavior Score was below 6,000, so chat/communication was locked entirely. Despite chat being locked, the communication reports kept coming in — coinciding precisely with matches in which I activated Smoke of Deceit. This confirms the smoke notification is being misattributed as my own communication. Match ID Matches for analysis: 8846190591 8846133477 8845268767 Timestamp when the bug occurs The issue triggers at the moment Smoke of Deceit is activated and the team-chat notification appears. See the timestamps of the smoke activations in the matches listed above. Steps to reproduce Use an account with text/voice communication restricted (Behavior Score below the communication threshold, no chat access). Enter a match and activate Smoke of Deceit. Observe the smoke-activation notification appearing in team chat. After the match, have another player submit a "communication abuse / text chat" report against the smoking player. The report is accepted and applied as a communication offense (column 12), despite the player having no chat or voice access and having sent no actual messages. Images and videos showing the bug I have attached my report statistics, which show communication-category reports (column 12) being applied during periods when chat was locked, alongside the general "Reports" metric (column 10) for comparison. Additional info Dotabuff profile: https://www.dotabuff.com/players/368512373 As a result of this bug I have received 5 reports, was placed in Low Priority, and lost Behavior/Conduct standing. Please review the report system: automated game notifications (such as Smoke of Deceit activation) must not be classified as player-authored communication, and players with restricted communication like to propose a clear, transparent mechanic for restoring Behavior Score one that is easy for every player to understand, beneficial for the entire community, and designed with anti-abuse safeguards in mind. The problem Losing Behavior Score is correctly designed to be quick, while regaining it is slow. However, the exact way to recover is currently unclear to most players. There are no visible, fixed parameters that guarantee progress, which leads to frustration and a sense of helplessness especially among those who ended up in low-priority or low-Behavior Score pools by accident. The proposal Make Single Draft games a predictable source of Behavior Score restoration. Specifically: +10 Behavior Score for any completed Single Draft match, regardless of outcome. +50 Behavior Score for a Single Draft win. This applies only to Single Draft games not already accounted for by the current system. Why these numbers Given that an average match already yields a small variable amount of Behavior Score through commend-based or time-based recovery, these fixed bonuses are small enough not to devalue positive conduct in other modes, yet meaningful enough to provide a visible, reliable path forward. The 5:1 ratio between a win and a loss maintains a healthy incentive to play seriously, while still acknowledging effort even in defeat. Why Single Draft It naturally pushes players out of their comfort zone, broadening hero pools and improving adaptability — this raises the general skill level of the player base. It acts as a fair recovery environment for players who were placed in low priority due to circumstances beyond their control (internet or power outages, emergency situations, etc.), without excusing genuinely disruptive behavior. Anti-abuse considerations To prevent exploitation (e.g., intentionally losing to farm Behavior Score), the bonus could be capped at a limited number of Single Draft games per day or per week. I just want to remind you that players have found a way to WATCH and even DOWNLOAD Immortal Draft matches they haven't even participated in. This is done through a feature that allows you to watch a friend's match. As soon as the match ends, everyone is taken to the match stats, but for some reason, this also happens for the **spectator**, allowing them to download a demo. Right now, dozens of matches are being watched in Immortal Draft online in order to be saved after their completion. The process is already automated, and it is now possible to search for matches from specific pro players. For now, everything is in the [Telegram channel](https://t.me/ProjectRelocate), but they are currently working on a public website with even more detailed statistics. ### You can simply download the required file and use the playdemo replays/id command to watch ANY match in Immortal Draft. ## ### What was the point of removing Immortal Draft matches from Dota TV, but leaving such a big hole that could be easily abused? You even banned players from viewing a friend's match history if friend is in Immortal Draft. ### Prevent friends from watching matches if a participant is in Immortal Draft, or at least prevent those who watched the match this way from downloading the demo. A compromise option: allow the Immortal Draft spectator to download no more than one demo per day from this mode. ##

Description I would like to raise a serious concern regarding the current role queue token system. At the moment, players receive 2 tokens for selecting positions 4 and 5, and 4 tokens for selecting all roles. This creates a fundamentally flawed incentive structure. Instead of encouraging players to fill less popular roles, it actively encourages them to select all roles purely to farm tokens. As a result, players are regularly assigned to roles they do not play or have no experience with. For example, support players are frequently placed into core roles such as mid or carry. In practice, this leads to severely compromised match quality. When a player is forced into an unfamiliar role—especially a high-impact role like mid—it often results in a one-sided game and, in many cases, a near-certain loss for their team. This is not an occasional issue, but a consistent and highly disruptive pattern. The current system effectively punishes players who specialize in specific roles and degrades the competitive integrity of matchmaking. A more effective approach would be to align token rewards with actual role demand. Less popular roles (such as position 5) should provide significantly higher rewards, while more popular roles should provide fewer. This would discourage token farming and ensure that players are more likely to play roles they are competent in. I would like to share some observations about the current Behavior Score and communication restriction system in Dota 2. I have been playing Dota since the Dota Allstars era (around 2004) and was also active during the time of dota-league.com, one of the earlier community platforms that already implemented matchmaking, reporting systems, and moderation. Having played the game for more than 20 years with very few breaks, I have followed the evolution of its systems quite closely. This post is not meant as a complaint, but rather as long-term player feedback about some interactions in the current system that may produce unintended effects on player behavior and match quality. Dota 2 relies heavily on coordination and information exchange between players. During matches, players often need to communicate things such as ultimate cooldowns, teleport cooldowns, buyback availability, or the need to delay a fight until certain abilities are available. These kinds of details can strongly influence the outcome of fights and objectives. When players receive communication restrictions due to Behavior Score penalties, it becomes difficult to communicate this type of information. As a result, teammates may misinterpret certain decisions during a match. For example, a player might not join a fight because abilities are on cooldown, because the engagement is clearly lost, or because positioning or farming for the next objective is the safer decision. Without communication, these decisions can easily appear as intentional non-cooperation. Reports are typically submitted during or immediately after matches. At that point, it may not yet be clear whether a decision that appeared questionable during the game was actually strategically correct. For instance, refusing to follow a teammate into a lost engagement may look negative in the moment but can later turn out to be the correct macro decision for the team. Because reports happen immediately, they can sometimes reflect frustration in the moment rather than an objective evaluation of behavior. When communication is limited, players also cannot explain their reasoning during the match. This may increase misunderstandings and lead to additional reports. I understand that Valve likely uses background systems to evaluate report accuracy over time, but restricted communication may still contribute to a feedback loop where misunderstandings increase reports and reports further reduce communication. From earlier community-run systems such as dota-league.com, reporting mechanisms also existed. Those systems were simpler and largely player-driven, but they often focused on clearly disruptive behavior. They also included moderation steps such as report reviews, cooldowns, temporary bans, and bans for multi-accounting to prevent players from bypassing penalties. While the system itself was simpler, enforcement against multi-accounting made it harder to circumvent the intended penalties. In the current environment, creating new accounts is relatively easy. While I understand that Dota 2 already has safeguards such as restricting ranked access for new accounts and estimating player skill before calibration matches, multi-accounting can still occur. Experienced players creating additional accounts can result in skill imbalances in matches. This may cause frustration among teammates and indirectly lead to toxicity or reports even when the underlying cause is the match imbalance rather than individual behavior. Another observation that may indicate unintended incentives relates to Low Priority Single Draft matches. Interestingly, some players report that these matches can sometimes feel less tense or less toxic than normal ranked games, even though they are intended as a penalty environment. From personal experience, I sometimes find Low Priority Single Draft games more enjoyable than regular ranked games, which seems paradoxical. I also know players who intentionally try to receive reports in order to play in Low Priority because they perceive those matches as less stressful than the normal Single Draft queue. If players intentionally attempt to enter Low Priority to access a different match environment, this may suggest that the system is producing unintended incentives. At the same time, intentionally steering accounts into Low Priority may further distort matchmaking and player behavior. Over the many years I have played Dota, it felt at certain points that the overall match environment was more balanced and less toxic. As someone who has followed the game for more than two decades, I find some of these developments unfortunate and would simply appreciate if this type of long-term player feedback could be considered during future improvements to the behavior and reporting systems. If you were just playing the game, just trying to win and doing everything you could, not destroying items, not interfering with your teammates’ chances to win, simply consistently trying to win, why do reports damage your behavior score?
